what_its_for: Fenfluramine is used to help reduce seizures in patients with Dravet syndrome, a rare and severe form of epilepsy. It works in the brain to help control abnormal electrical activity that causes seizures.
how_to_take: Take fenfluramine by mouth as a liquid (oral solution) exactly as your doctor tells you. Use the measuring device that comes with the medicine to measure the correct dose — do not use a household spoon. You can take it with or without food. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. Swallow it right after measuring.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time based on how well it works and how you tolerate it. The typical starting dose is very small and is adjusted based on your body weight. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can make seizures worse.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fenfluramine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Do not freeze or refrigerate. Keep it away from light and out of reach of children. Use the solution within 90 days of first opening the bottle. This medication is kept in a special locked program — your pharmacy will provide it through a certified program only.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase side effects and make you more drowsy. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially other seizure medicines like valproate or stiripentol, as they can interact with fenfluramine and may require a dose change.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: decreased appetite or significant weight loss, unusual tiredness or weakness, feeling sad, depressed, or having thoughts of self-harm, fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, swelling in your legs or ankles, or if seizures get worse. Seek emergency help immediately if you have trouble breathing or chest pain. This medicine requires regular heart checkups (echocardiograms) to monitor your heart valves and blood pressure in the lungs.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks before you notice a reduction in seizures. Do not stop taking the medicine if you do not see results right away. Your doctor will monitor your progress and adjust the dose as needed. Most patients see a benefit within the first few months of treatment.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is approved for use in children 2 years of age and older. Doses are based on body weight. Elderly: There is limited information about use in older adults; use with caution. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as the risks are not fully known. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
